We had a bug report that xfstest generic/355 was failing on NFSv4.0.
This test sets various combinations of setuid/setgid modes and tests
whether DIO writes will cause them to be stripped.
What I found was that the server did properly strip those bits
the client didn't notice because it held a delegation that was not
recalled. The recall didn't occur because the client itself was the
one generating the activity and we avoid recalls in that case.
Clearing setuid bits is an ""implicit"" activity. The client didn't
specifically request that we do that
column2: so we need the server to issue a

column1: CB_RECALL
column2: or avoid the situation entirely by not issuing a delegation.

column1: The easiest fix here is to simply not give out a delegation if the file
is being opened for write
column2: and the mode has the setuid and/or setgid bit

column1: set. Note that there is a potential race between the mode and lease
being set
column2: so we test for this condition both before and after setting

column1: the lease.
This patch fixes generic/355
